about: The org chart formula's data: the teams in output order, each seat's id, title, template, department, reason and manager, the channel list, the default channels, the phrases the reasons are made of and the limits. chart_formula.py builds the chart from this file and holds the rules; nothing here is logic. A seat with `per` is made once for each picked segment (`segment`), picked channel (`channel`), initiative (`initiative`) or industry Owner (`industry`); a seat with `unless` is made only when nothing was picked for it (`segment`: no segment picked). `live` says the seat starts with a bot at setup: true for every seat it is on, "first" for the first picked segment's seat only. Placeholders are filled in by chart_formula.py, in one pass: {label} is a segment's or initiative's short label, {seg} a segment's id part, {initiatives} the initiatives a product owner's segment owns, {ref} the bet id an initiative Owner's reason names, {statement} the bet's statement, {title} and {topic} an industry Owner's title and its topic.
rules: Cross-language rules: the JS port must match the chart byte for byte. A length counts Unicode code points (JS [...s].length). Whitespace is the ASCII set space, tab, line feed, carriage return, form feed and vertical tab: each run becomes one space, and none is kept at either end. Names are compared by lower() (JS toLowerCase), never casefold(), and only to tell names apart. An id is a slug of a-z and 0-9: every other run of characters becomes one '-', none at either end, and 'x' when nothing is left. Placeholders are filled in one pass, so a name that contains braces is only text. A reason quotes a label with curly quotes.
